scene.description: Two cut-paper browser-window cards stand side by side on a pale plinth, one built from a single flat sheet and one built from several visibly layered sheets, a small navy paper fork-shaped junction sitting between them and glowing faintly from beneath.
scene.one_idea: two build approaches sitting at one decision point

objects.state: built from a single flat sheet, standing at the left, unlit
objects.prop_definition: rounded rectangle of card stock, raised raised top strip cut from warm grey card, matte paper, never metal or gloss with slotted address bar and punched dots, recessed content panel

objects.state: built from several visibly stacked layers of card, standing at the right, unlit
sitting on the plinth between the two cards, glowing faintly from beneath, the one lit element in the frame

lighting.key: soft warm key light, upper left, 3000K to 3500K, roughly 40 degrees, large diffuser, soft gradual shadow edges
lighting.fill: weak cool fill from the right, about one quarter key strength
lighting.practical: single internal practical beneath the navy junction, glowing at #FDE7C8, spilling onto both cards evenly

camera.setup: A: three-quarter elevated, 30 to 40 degrees above the plane, wide enough to show both cards and the junction between them
camera.focus: sharp on the junction and both cards
camera.framing: approximately 45 to 55 degree horizontal field of view, moderate compression, focal group sharp, background softly defocused

background.falloff: darker toward the top of the frame

composition_rules.focal_position: centred between the two cards, cards themselves off to either third
composition_rules.physical_plausibility: every object must be able to stand, lean or lie as shown
composition_rules.neutrality_note: neither card is presented as the winner; both remain unlit and equal, only the decision point itself is lit
composition_rules.one_focal_group: exactly one warm-lit focal group with a single light source: the navy junction, the one lit element
composition_rules.navy_group_rule: the navy element is one object, or repetitions of one identical object in one contiguous composition; never mixed navy objects
composition_rules.navy_range: subdued navy paper only, #1A2340 to #3F4A68; no vivid, emitted or periwinkle blue

negative: Google or browser or search-engine marks
more than one warm light source
more than one navy element group
